slides.title: Web and File Transfer Protocols
slides.body:
File Transfer Protocols: FTP
FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol
It is a standard network protocol used to transfer files between a client and a server over the internet
client 
server
FTPS / SFTP are secure variations used in modern systems

slides.title: Web and File Transfer Protocols
slides.body:
How Does FTP Work?
Two types of FTP connections:
Passive mode
Active mode
Server connects to the client to transfer data
Client connects to the server for data transfer

slides.title: Web and File Transfer Protocols
slides.body:
FTP Functions
Upload Files: Send files from your computer to the server
Download Files: Retrieve files from the server to your computer
Manage Files: You can rename, delete, or organize files on the server

It defines how different software applications can interact with each other, request data, and exchange information

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
Understanding HTTP
HTTP: The standard protocol for data exchange on the internet
Every web interaction (e.g., browsing, clicking, submitting forms) involves sending an HTTP request and receiving a response
The Foundation of Web Communication

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body: Structure of an HTTP Request

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
Anatomy of an HTTP Request
Body:  The actual data sent with an HTTP request, usually in POST or PUT methods (e.g., JSON, HTML, text, images, files).

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
HTTP Request Analogy
Header:
Content-Type: Specifies the kind of pizza being ordered. For example, "large cheese pizza" or "veggie pizza."
Authorization: Here is my payment token to authorize the order
Accept: Type of pizza or delivery. E.g. "vegetarian pizza" or "delivery”

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
Example –Get Products API
Method: GET → Fetch product details (no changes)
URL: https://example.com/products → Server address holding product info
Headers: Accept: application/json → Expect response in JSON format
Body: Usually empty for GET requests (only fetching data)

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body: Structure of an HTTP Response

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
Anatomy of an HTTP Response
Body: Contains the actual content returned by the server (e.g., JSON, HTML, text, images, files, etc.)
Status Code: Indicates the result of the request
200 OK: Successful request
404 Not Found: The requested resource does not exist

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
HTTP Response Analogy
Body: Your order for a large cheese pizza with extra olives is confirmed and will be delivered to 123 Pizza Street. Thank you for your order
Status Code: Your pizza order has been successfully received and confirmed
200 OK: Successful request
404 Not Found: The pizza you requested is not available

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
Example - searching for a product
Status Code: 
200 OK: The request was successful, and the product details have been returned
Headers:
Content-Type: application/json
Indicates that the response is in JSON format
Cache-Control: no-cache
Ensures that the response is not cached

slides.title: Web Communication: APIs
slides.body:
Why Understanding HTTP Matters ?
HTTP structure powers web apps
Key components: Method, URL, Headers, Body, Status Codes
Foundation for REST APIs, enabling seamless, scalable, and interactive web apps
